content:
I've been experimenting with merge queues, and enabled bors for Tau Ceti. It's set up so a single configuration variable allows us to switch back and forth (it waits for the old queue to drain before starting the other one), and I'm intending to run some experiments over the next few days to see which one is actually better. I'm hopeful that bors will be quite a bit more efficient, reducing our CI costs at little expense on latency.

(For background, bors takes several ready-to-merge PRs and just runs CI once on a staging branch combining all of them. If that passes, they then land on the default branch together. Each PR still gets a separate commit, but there is no guarantee that each commit is individually green. If the combination fails, then bors automatically bisects.)

@Kim Morrison Some PRs seem to have been stranded when the merge queue switched back to the default (they've shown bors=PENDING for 18-20 hours). #12504 is an example, but there are many more (11 total of mine; I'm not sure how many of others'). Others show bors=FAILURE (e.g. #12351) but are labeled as ready-to-merge.

Yep, investigating this now.

The initial experiments suggest bors is a success, reducing time spent in merge queue CI by a factor of about 4x.

But that doesn't count if we can't reliably get everything in.

bors seems to be reporting false "Merge conflict" failures, and nothing has merged since 07:55 UTC.

Example: #12808 (head df30b3cb0, rebased on main this morning) failed in bors batches 150 and 158 with "Merge conflict", after batch 144 was canceled. It merges cleanly into current main: git merge-tree shows no conflicts and GitHub reports it MERGEABLE.

Several other ready-to-merge PRs have the same bors status, most of them single-commit PRs: #13126, #13132–#13135, #13138, #13140, #13143, #13146, #13148, #13151.

Could bors be reporting a conflict between PRs in the same batch as a conflict for every member of that batch? Or is something else stuck after the switch from the GitHub merge queue?

I think this is not actually a problem, just bors' reporting not being that great. I think your last

Tavi said:

Could bors be reporting a conflict between PRs in the same batch as a conflict for every member of that batch?

is correct, but also that this is "self-healing" and bors eventually sorts this out. I agree it is not great, as it is confusing if you're looking at the state of the PRs. (I recall this happening at Mathlib.)

The good news is that we are running our own fork of bors, so can perhaps change the behaviour here.

My preference is to get the actually critical problems sorted out, and the merge queue drained, before dealing with these "cosmetic" problems. (Unless it turns out to be more than cosmetic!)

Thanks, that makes sense. One correction to my first message: bors was merging normally all along. It closes PRs rather than marking them merged, and I missed that, so "nothing has merged since 07:55" was wrong. I had already squashed #12808 (it contained an empty "re-trigger CI" commit) before seeing your reply. The content is unchanged, so it will just go through CI and review again. From now on I'll leave "Merge conflict" PRs alone and let bors sort them out.

I can view the link; on the first visit, github auth would be required (one of the permissions is to act on the user's behalf :fear: ). You may have refused the github auth, causing unauthorized ?
(By the way, what's the advantage of bors over GitHub merge queue? The bors homepage says it's deprecated and user should use GitHub merge queue instead, unless self-hosted)

It redirects me to https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize?client_id=............&redirect_uri=&response_type=code but then I get a 404 page, which I guess is GitHub's way to showing permission denied)
Already tried with clearing cache and such, doesn't help.

user202729 said:

(By the way, what's the advantage of bors over GitHub merge queue? The bors homepage says it's deprecated and user should use GitHub merge queue instead, unless self-hosted)

See #mathlib4 > Purpose of Bors for specifics . My impression at the time is that GitHub merge queue is a feature incomplete product inspired by bors, and mathlib maintainers determined that GitHub merge queue is insuffcient for coping with the high and heavy traffic of mathlib PRs after initial discussions and small scale expreiments, so mathlib stayed and turned to self-hosting bors. It's natural for Tau Ceti to experiment with GitHub merge queue at scale in its infancy, but bors is better suited in the long term.
